premise.claim: A RoleBasedGroupSet propagates spec.groupTemplate to its children un-paced: 'when the template changes, every outdated child is updated within a single reconcile, with no ordering and no availability gating. For a set of N groups that means all N groups can restart at once — availability might drop to zero for the whole set.' (PR body, Motivation)
premise.evidence: base fc201cdf: Reconcile_OptimizedOrder updates all children in one pass (results/unit-base-p0.txt); live base binary on the fresh ACK cluster: both children carried the new template within 1s of the patch and readyGroups dropped to 0 for 3s (results/base-timeline.log); head binary paced the same change: demo-1 deleted 20:47:01.5, demo-0 at 20:47:05.9 after demo-1 was Ready, readyGroups never below 1 (results/head-timeline.log)

match: F1: spec.rolloutStrategy survives a v1alpha1 read-modify-write round trip
findings.note: v1alpha1<->v1alpha2 conversion drops spec.rolloutStrategy (+ new status counters); any v1alpha1 full-object write silently reverts a rolling set to the un-paced static behavior.

match: F2: an update that newly enables scalingAdapter is rejected
findings.note: the scalingAdapter-in-groupTemplate guard is create-only; an update that newly enables it is accepted, reaching the non-converging state the rule exists to prevent. Compat pinned by TestVerifyPR474_UpdateOnSetAlreadyCarryingAdapterAllowed (must stay green).
re-check of round-1 blocker: replicas-only diff on a legacy-spelling child must scale in place. PASSES on head (fixed).

match: F5: negative rollout budgets are rejected
findings.note: webhook accepts negative maxSurge/maxUnavailable/partition; maxUnavailable=-1 with maxSurge>0 wedges the rollout forever (budget=-1+readySurge=0, no delete ever issued), see canary below.
canary asserting the current stall: PASS today; flips when negative budgets are rejected/clamped.

partition>0 + held-back group not serving: rolloutComplete() requires ALL base serving so surge is never reclaimed, while the Rolling status condition reports RolloutComplete (held-back ordinals count in neither current nor updatedReady). Canary pins the mismatch.
while paused, a replicas-only in-place scale also syncs template labels/annotations, contradicting 'paused freezes template propagation'. Canary pins it.

P1 (second reviewer, independently confirmed): surge reclaimed earlier in the same reconcile still counts in the delete budget (readySurge reads the pre-reclaim snapshot). 3 serving base + 1 ready surge + maxUnavailable=1 + maxSurge 1->0: surge deleted, then TWO serving base groups deleted, leaving 1 serving instead of >=2. RED on head; green with children.surge = keptSurge after reclamation.

P1 (second reviewer, independently confirmed): a retained surge group is never reconciled against subsequent template changes (classifyRolloutChildren covers base only, warmUp only fills missing ordinals). maxUnavailable=0 + surge stuck unready on a superseded template -> budget stays 0 -> rollout wedges even after the template is corrected; standing canary (partition==replicas) also stalls on the old template. RED on head.

P1 (second reviewer, independently confirmed): the budget-exhausted `break` skips lower-ordinal not-serving outdated groups that the PR documents as free to replace. s-2 serving/budget-blocked + s-1 stuck unready on a bad template -> s-1 never repaired -> permanent wedge (the rollback never happens). RED on head; green with break -> continue (existing PR tests still pass under it).

liveNote: L3 ran on a dedicated ACK cluster (3 nodes, v1.36-aliyun) reached via the remote sandbox: PR CRDs + chart-installed webhook stack; in-cluster controller scaled to 0 while the head/base binaries ran out-of-cluster on the sandbox (v1alpha1-conversion F1 test ran first with the in-cluster webhook up). The e2e window additionally drops CRD conversion to None because the e2e framework's AfterEach issues v1alpha1 DeleteAllOf calls that a dead conversion webhook would fail.
